title: Personal, real and nominal accounts and the golden rules
summary: Sorting accounts into three families and applying one debit and credit rule to each, with the Northstar Bike Co. examples.

chunks.heading: Three families of accounts
chunks.explanation_md:
The traditional approach sorts every ledger account into one of three families. **The family decides the debit and credit rule.**

- **Personal accounts:** people, firms and organizations. Examples: debtors, creditors, banks, capital, individuals.
- **Real accounts:** assets the business owns. Examples: cash, inventory, equipment, buildings, goodwill.
- **Nominal accounts:** income and expenses for the period. Examples: rent, salaries, sales, commission, interest.

key_terms.meaning: An account for people, firms and organizations the business deals with.
An account for assets the business owns.
An account for income and expenses for the period.

chunks.heading: Personal accounts: debit the receiver, credit the giver
chunks.explanation_md:
For a **personal account** the golden rule is **Debit the receiver, Credit the giver.**

Example from the slide: Northstar Bike Co. pays **$500 cash to a supplier, Metro Parts Ltd.** The supplier receives the money, so **Metro Parts Ltd. is debited $500**. Cash is the giver, so **Cash A/c is credited $500**.

Common personal accounts: Debtors, Creditors, Capital, Bank A/c and Drawings.

chunks.heading: Real accounts: debit what comes in, credit what goes out
chunks.explanation_md:
For a **real account** the golden rule is **Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out.**

Example from the slide: Northstar Bike Co. buys a **repair stand for $1,200 cash.** The equipment comes in, so **Equipment A/c is debited $1,200**. Cash goes out, so **Cash A/c is credited $1,200**.

Common real accounts: Cash, Inventory, Equipment, Buildings and Goodwill.

chunks.heading: Nominal accounts: debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains
chunks.explanation_md:
For a **nominal account** the golden rule is **Debit all expenses and losses, Credit all incomes and gains.**

Example from the slide: Northstar Bike Co. pays **$300 cash for shop rent.** Rent is an expense, so **Rent A/c is debited $300**. Cash is the giver, so **Cash A/c is credited $300**.

Common nominal accounts: Rent, Salaries, Sales, Commission and Interest.

chunks.heading: The three golden rules in one table
chunks.explanation_md:
| Account type | Covers | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Personal | People, firms, banks | The receiver | The giver |
| Real | Assets the business owns | What comes in | What goes out |
| Nominal | Income and expenses | Expenses and losses | Incomes and gains |

The slide says: **one classification, one rule**. Every transaction fits exactly one row per account touched.

So for each transaction: (1) find the accounts, (2) classify each as personal, real or nominal, (3) apply its rule. The debit and credit will then balance.

chunks.heading: Applying the rules: three Northstar Bike Co. entries
chunks.explanation_md:
Three transactions, three account types, one balanced journal:

- **Real:** buys a delivery van for $32,000 cash. **Dr Delivery Van A/c $32,000, Cr Cash A/c $32,000.** The van comes in (Dr); cash goes out (Cr).
- **Personal:** receives $2,000 cash from customer Alex Rivera. **Dr Cash A/c $2,000, Cr Alex Rivera A/c $2,000.** Cash comes in (Dr); Rivera is the giver (Cr).
- **Nominal:** pays $150 cash for shop electricity. **Dr Electricity Exp. A/c $150, Cr Cash A/c $150.** The expense is incurred (Dr); cash is the giver (Cr).

Notice that cash is an asset (real account) but it can appear on either side, depending on whether it comes in or goes out.
chunks.exam_line: Delivery van: Dr Van, Cr Cash. Cash from Alex Rivera: Dr Cash, Cr Rivera. Electricity: Dr Electricity Exp., Cr Cash.

questions.stem: Differentiate between how real accounts and nominal accounts are debited and credited.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Real accounts** cover assets the business owns (cash, inventory, equipment, buildings, goodwill). Rule: debit what comes in, credit what goes out. Example: buying a delivery van for $32,000 cash debits Delivery Van A/c and credits Cash A/c.

**Nominal accounts** cover income and expenses for the period (rent, salaries, sales, commission, interest). Rule: debit all expenses and losses, credit all incomes and gains. Example: paying $150 for electricity debits Electricity Exp. A/c.

rubric.point: Real covers assets owned; nominal income and expenses

questions.stem: Explain the three golden rules of debit and credit. Apply them to the three Northstar Bike Co. transactions: a $32,000 delivery van for cash, $2,000 received from Alex Rivera, and $150 paid for electricity.
questions.model_answer_md:
Accounts are first classified as **personal, real or nominal**, and the type decides the rule.

| Type | Debit | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| Personal | The receiver | The giver |
| Real | What comes in | What goes out |
| Nominal | Expenses and losses | Incomes and gains |

**1. Delivery van, $32,000 cash (real):** the van comes in and cash goes out. Dr Delivery Van A/c $32,000, Cr Cash A/c $32,000.

**2. $2,000 from customer Alex Rivera (personal):** cash comes in (Dr) and Rivera is the giver (Cr). Dr Cash A/c $2,000, Cr Alex Rivera A/c $2,000.

**3. $150 for shop electricity (nominal):** an expense is incurred (Dr) and cash is the giver (Cr). Dr Electricity Exp. A/c $150, Cr Cash A/c $150.

In each entry the debit equals the credit, so the journal stays balanced.

questions.stem: For each of the following Northstar Bike Co. transactions, classify the accounts and give the journal entry: (a) $500 cash paid to supplier Metro Parts Ltd., (b) a repair stand bought for $1,200 cash, (c) $300 cash paid for shop rent.
questions.model_answer_md:
**(a) $500 paid to Metro Parts Ltd.** Metro Parts Ltd. is a personal account and is the receiver, so it is debited. Cash is the giver and is credited. **Dr Metro Parts Ltd. $500, Cr Cash A/c $500.**

**(b) Repair stand for $1,200.** Equipment is a real account and comes in, so it is debited. Cash goes out and is credited. **Dr Equipment A/c $1,200, Cr Cash A/c $1,200.**

**(c) Shop rent $300.** Rent is a nominal account and an expense, so it is debited. Cash is the giver and is credited. **Dr Rent A/c $300, Cr Cash A/c $300.**

In all three, Cash is credited because cash goes out, but the debited account follows the rule of its own type.

rubric.point: Metro Parts: personal, receiver, Dr; Cash Cr $500
Repair stand: real, comes in, Dr Equipment $1,200
Cash is credited in all three, amounts equal
